CoreCUCS1002

Data Structures with Competitive Coding

Syllabus

Faculty: Dr. Sasmita Kumari Nayak
Course Name : Data Structures with Competitive Coding
Code(Credit) : CUCS1002 (2-4-0)
Course Objectives
  • To train students in algorithm analysis, recursion, and selecting suitable data structures for problem-solving, focusing on algorithm correctness.
  • To implement dynamic data structures (linked lists, binary trees) and sub-quadratic sorting algorithms (quick sort, merge sort, heap sort) to solve data structure problems.
  • To analyze and compare data structure performance, evaluate algorithmic efficiency, and solve competitive coding problems while developing industry‑ready skills through practical application of data structures.

Course Outcomes:
After the completion of the course students will be able to:
  • CO1:Recall and identify fundamental algorithmic techniques, recursive methods, and data structure concepts to explain algorithm correctness and complexity analysis.
  • CO2:Explain and interpret dynamic data structures (linked lists, stacks, queues, trees) and describe their operations for efficient data manipulation and storage.
  • CO3:Implement and execute sorting, searching algorithms, and graph traversal techniques to solve computational problems with sub-quadratic performance.
  • CO4:Analyze and compare advanced data structures (hashing, heaps, balanced trees) and evaluate their efficiency in solving timed competitive coding problems.
  • CO5:Evaluate and justify the selection of appropriate data structures and algorithms for software development scenarios, assessing trade-offs to demonstrate readiness for industry roles.

Course Syllabus:

Module 1: Data Structures Basics (10 hours)
Theory
  • Definition, Importance of data structures, Algorithm definition, and Pseudocode
  • Types of Data Structures, Abstract Data Types (ADTs)
  • Complexity Analysis and Asymptotic Notations

Module 2: Arrays, Stacks and Queues (25 hours)
Theory
  • Arrays and its operations
  • Stack Operations and Applications
  • Queue Operations and Applications
  • Variants: Circular Queue, Priority Queue, Deque
 Practice
  • Experiment 2.1: Implement a program to demonstrate the use of arrays.
  • Experiment 2.2: Implement a program to perform insertion and deletion operations on an array.
  • Experiment 2.3: Implement a singly linked list.
  • Experiment 2.4: Execute insertion and deletion operations on a singly linked list.
  • Experiment 2.5: Implement a doubly linked list.
  • Experiment 2.6: Implement a program to perform insertion and deletion operations on a doubly linked list.
  • Experiment 2.7: Implement a circular linked list.
  • Experiment 2.8: Execute insertion and deletion operations on a circular linked list.
  • Experiment 2.9: Implement a program to reverse a linked list.
  • Experiment 2.10: Implement a program to merge two sorted linked lists.
 
Module 3: Linked Lists (15 hours)
Theory
  • Linked Lists: Singly, Doubly, Circular
  • Operations on Linked Lists: Insert, Delete, Search, Sort, Reverse, Merge
 Practice
  • Experiment 3.1: Implement a stack using an array.
  • Experiment 3.2: Implement a program to perform push and pop operations on a stack.
  • Experiment 3.3: Implement a queue using an array.
  • Experiment 3.4: Execute enqueue and dequeue operations on a queue.
  • Experiment 3.5: Implement a circular queue.
  • Experiment 3.6: Execute insertion and deletion operations on a circular queue.
  • Experiment 3.7: Implement a priority queue.
  • Experiment 3.8: Execute insertion and deletion operations on a priority queue.
 
Module 4: Trees and Recursion (30 hours)
Theory
  • Explain Recursion in detail: Stack frames used to implement recursion internally.
  • Binary Trees: Representation, Traversals, and Operations.
  • Binary Search Trees (BST): Search, Insertion, and Deletion Operations.
  • Balanced Trees: AVL Trees, Balancing Operations, and Red-Black Trees.
 Practice
  • Experiment 4.1: Implement a binary tree.
  • Experiment 4.2: Implement a program to perform inorder, preorder, and postorder traversals on a binary tree.
  • Experiment 4.3: Implement a program to compute the height of a binary tree.
  • Experiment 4.4: Implement a Binary Search Tree (BST).
  • Experiment 4.5: Execute insertion and deletion operations on a Binary Search Tree (BST).
  • Experiment 4.6: Implement an AVL tree.
  • Experiment 4.7: Execute and examine insertion and deletion operations on an AVL tree using rotations.
  • Experiment 4.8: Implement a Red-Black tree.
 
Module 5: Graphs (20 hours)
Theory
  • Introduction to Graphs and examples of real-world situations modeled as equivalent graph problems.
  • Graph Traversal: Depth First Search (DFS) and Breadth First Search (BFS).
  • Topological Sorting.
  • Shortest Path Algorithms: Floyd-Warshall Algorithm.
 Practice
  • Experiment 5.1: Implement a graph using an adjacency matrix.
  • Experiment 5.2: Implement a graph using an adjacency list.
  • Experiment 5.3: Execute Breadth-First Search (BFS) traversal on a graph.
  • Experiment 5.4: Execute Depth-First Search (DFS) traversal on a graph.
  • Experiment 5.5: Implement and analyze the shortest path in a graph using Dijkstra's algorithm.
  • Experiment 5.6: Implement and analyze the shortest path in a graph using the Floyd-Warshall algorithm.
  • Experiment 5.7: Implement a program to find the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of a graph using Kruskal's algorithm.
  • Experiment 5.8: Implement a program to find the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of a graph using Prim's algorithm.
 
Module 6: Hashing and Heaps (20 hours)
Theory
  • Hash Tables: Hash Functions and Collision Handling.
  • Heaps: Min-Heap, Max-Heap, and Heap Operations.
 Practice
  • Experiment 6.1: Implement a hash table with a suitable hash function.
  • Experiment 6.2: Implement collision handling using chaining.
  • Experiment 6.3: Implement collision handling using open addressing and compare both strategies.
  • Experiment 6.4: Implement a min-heap.
  • Experiment 6.5: Implement a program to perform insertion and deletion operations on a min-heap.
  • Experiment 6.6: Implement a max-heap.
  • Experiment 6.7: Execute insertion and deletion operations on a max-heap.
  • Experiment 6.8: Implement heap sort and evaluate its performance with comparison-based sorting algorithms.
 
Module 7: Sorting and Searching (20 hours)
Theory
  • Linear Search, Binary Search, and Time Complexity Analysis.
  • Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort, and Time Complexity Analysis.
  • Merge Sort, Quick Sort, and Time Complexity Analysis.
Practice
  • Experiment 7.1: Implement linear search and test its performance on various dataset sizes.
  • Experiment 7.2: Implement binary search and compare its performance with linear search.
  • Experiment 7.3: Implement bubble sort.
  • Experiment 7.4: Implement selection sort.
  • Experiment 7.5: Implement insertion sort.
  • Experiment 7.6: Implement quick sort with different pivot selection strategies and analyze its performance.
  • Experiment 7.7: Implement merge sort and compare its performance with quick sort for different input types.
  • Experiment 7.8: Implement a program to perform Radix sort.
 Text Books:
  1. "Schaum’s outline of theory and Problems of data structures." by Lipschutz, S.
Reference Books:     
  1.  "Fundamentals of Data Structures in C", 2nd Edition, E. Horowitz, S. Sahni and Susan Anderson Freed, Universities Press.  
  2. "Data Structures using C – A. S. Tanenbaum, Y. Langsam, and M.J.Augenstein, PHI/Pearson Education.    
  3. " Data Structures: A Pseudocode Approach with C" , 2nd Edition, R. F. Gilberg and B.A. Forouzan, Cengage Learning. 
  4. "Data Structures Using C." by Alok Kumar Jagadev (Author), Amiya Kumar Rath
